evidence: "m = n-1"; "It is guaranteed that if all m available procedures were executed, the relative differences between all n sensors would be fully determined"; both survivors build adjacency lists and root/traverse the graph
affordance_in_statement: The input has m = n - 1 procedures, and all procedures together determine the relative differences between all n sensors.
removal_suggestion: There is no legal wording-only removal: with n-1 procedures and full determination of all sensors, the procedure graph is necessarily a connected tree. Defeating this approach would require changing the underlying scenario to permit redundant/cyclic procedures, such as allowing more than n-1 procedures, which is prohibited here.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the input graph as a tree and solves the minimum-weight subtree containing the primary sensors by rooting from a primary.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: "m = n - 1" together with the full-determination guarantee; solution text says "Root at first primary" and constructs an adjacency list.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the tree structure so only the unique paths connecting primary sensors need to be paid for.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The solution explicitly comments "m equals n-1" and builds an undirected adjacency list for tree traversal.

common_affordance: The procedure graph is forced to be a connected weighted tree, so every required primary-to-primary relation has a unique path and the answer is the weight of the union of those paths.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DSU/Kruskal-style treatment models the task as generic edge selection or terminal connectivity and does not correctly account for the complete union of mandatory non-primary bridge edges in the tree.
It sorts edges and applies a generic union-find connectivity strategy, which can omit or misprice Steiner-path edges that are necessary even though they do not directly join two primary sensors.

recommended_edit: No permitted edit can defeat both surviving solutions while preserving the immutable constraints. If the scenario may be changed, allow redundant calibration procedures/cycles by permitting more than n-1 procedures; otherwise the tree reduction is an unavoidable structural consequence.
regression_risk: Changing the graph model to a general cyclic graph could restore the already-defeated DSU-based solutions on some cases, so regression tests would be needed.
